title: From 5G to NearLink: Europe’s next digital dependency risk
gist: China's Huawei-developed NearLink wireless protocol (star successor to Bluetooth/WiFi) is quietly spreading into Europe via imported smartphones, wearables and industrial modules, creating a diffuse dependency risk that MERICS analyst Jeroen Groenewegen-Lau says the EU can still manage using existing but under-used regulatory tools like the Digital Networks Act and Cyber Resilience Act.

insights.claim: Less than a decade after confronting the risks of relying on Huawei and ZTE for 5G networks, Europe is drifting into a new Chinese technology dependence that is more diffuse and harder to detect.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Investors and policymakers tracking EU tech-sovereignty regulation should expect a new wave of scrutiny on Chinese short-range wireless components, echoing the Huawei 5G ban precedent.
insights.quote: Less than a decade after Europe had to confront the risks of relying on Huawei, ZTE and other Chinese telecom equipment makers for its 5G networks, it is drifting into a new dependence that is more diffuse and harder to detect.
insights.locator: From 5G to NearLink: Europe's next digital dependency risk

insights.claim: NearLink (also known as SparkLink, Chinese: 星闪), positioned as China's alternative to Bluetooth and WiFi, is entering Europe through imported smartphones, wearables like fitness trackers, digital keys and industrial control modules, creating potential lock-in effects.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Component makers and device OEMs selling into Europe should watch for embedded NearLink modules becoming a compliance and supply-chain disclosure issue.
insights.quote: NearLink (星闪, also known as SparkLink), China’s alternative to Bluetooth and WiFi, is entering Europe through imported smartphones, wearable devices like fitness trackers, digital keys and industrial control modules – creating potential lock in effects that could make European companies and consumers increasingly reliant on this technology long before regulators respond.
insights.locator: Less than a decade after Europe had to confront

insights.claim: NearLink combines the low-power advantages of Bluetooth with the high-throughput capabilities of Wi-Fi to support thousands of connected devices simultaneously, and peer-reviewed studies support its adoption where performance matters.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: The technology has genuine performance advantages, meaning bans are less straightforward than with 5G infrastructure and adoption pressure will persist regardless of regulatory concerns.
insights.quote: Peer-reviewed studies back the case for adoption where performance matters.
insights.locator: Beijing is positioning NearLink as a new generation

insights.claim: Beyond consumer devices, Chinese state-linked initiatives are pushing NearLink into robotics and aerospace, while official standard-setting efforts target anti-quantum cryptography and civil drone identification.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: NearLink's ambitions extend well beyond wearables into strategic sectors like drones and cryptography standards, widening the surface area for future export-control or standards disputes.
insights.quote: Chinese state linked initiatives are pushing NearLink into areas like robotics and aerospace, while official standard-setting efforts are eyeing areas like anti quantum cryptography and civil drone identification.
insights.locator: Beijing is positioning NearLink as a new generation

themes.theme: Why NearLink is structurally different from the Huawei 5G threat

insights.claim: Unlike Huawei's role in 5G, which placed Chinese technology at key nodes of centralized communications networks, NearLink enters Europe through the far more distributed layer of individual connected products and components, making it harder to monitor or regulate.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Regulators cannot rely on the same chokepoint-based interventions used against Huawei's 5G infrastructure; a different, component-level governance approach is needed.
insights.quote: Unlike Huawei’s role in 5G, which placed Chinese technology at key nodes of communications networks, NearLink is entering Europe through the more distributed layer of connected products and components.
insights.locator: NearLink is not just another ordinary wireless protocol

insights.claim: As the number of devices using NearLink increases, the technology will handle an ever-growing volume of security-critical data flows across Europe.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: The risk compounds over time as adoption scales, meaning early intervention is cheaper than waiting for critical mass to be reached.
insights.quote: As the number of devices using Nearlink increases, the technology will handle ever more security critical data flows.
insights.locator: NearLink is not just another ordinary wireless protocol

themes.theme: China's tech self-reliance drive and NearLink's origins

insights.claim: NearLink is a product of the tech decoupling between China and the US, developed by Huawei after it was expelled from the Wi-Fi Alliance and Bluetooth Special Interest Group in 2019 following US sanctions, and framed by Beijing as vital to China's digital sovereignty.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: NearLink's origin story shows it is a direct, durable consequence of US sanctions policy on Huawei, suggesting the technology's push into global markets will continue regardless of near-term diplomatic shifts.
insights.quote: Huawei began developing the technology after it was expelled from the Wi Fi Alliance and Bluetooth Special Interest Group in 2019 after it came under US sanctions and framed its efforts as vital to China's digital sovereignty.
insights.locator: It is another element in China’s drive for technological self-reliance

insights.claim: NearLink follows the same self-reliance logic as China's home-grown mobile network standards, the failed WAPI alternative to Wi-Fi, the BeiDou satellite navigation system built as a GPS counterpart, and the proposed NewIP internet protocol.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: NearLink sits within a recurring Chinese playbook of parallel technical standards; its outcome can be benchmarked against WAPI's failure versus BeiDou's success to gauge likely trajectory.
insights.quote: The same logic has driven China’s development of home-grown mobile network standards, the ill fated WAPI alternative to Wi Fi, the BeiDou satellite navigation system as a counterpart to GPS, and proposals such as NewIP for future internet protocols.
insights.locator: It is another element in China’s drive for technological self-reliance

themes.theme: Huawei's international expansion playbook for NearLink

insights.claim: Huawei set up the International SparkLink Wireless Short Range Communication Alliance (iSLA) in 2020 and first deployed NearLink commercially in its Mate 60 series phone in August 2023.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Timeline shows NearLink moved from alliance formation to commercial deployment in three years, indicating a fast, well-resourced rollout that could similarly accelerate abroad.
insights.quote: The company set up the International SparkLink Wireless Short Range Communication Alliance (iSLA) in 2020 and first deployed Nearlink commercially in its Mate 60 series phone in August 2023.
insights.locator: Huawei is seeking recognition for the technology as a global standard

insights.claim: Huawei embedded NearLink in its HarmonyOS 5 operating system in November 2024 to draw in the software developer community, and by 2025 iSLA reported over 100 million NearLink devices shipped, backed by more than 1,200 alliance members, 600 products and over 300 chip and module development boards.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: The scale of the ecosystem (100M+ devices, 1,200+ alliance members) signals NearLink has already crossed from experimental to mass-market status, raising the cost and urgency of any later European intervention.
insights.quote: in 2025, iSLA reported that over a 100 million NearLink devices had been shipped, backed by over 1,200 alliance members, 600 products, and 300 plus chip and module development boards that help companies create more products.
insights.locator: Huawei is seeking recognition for the technology as a global standard

insights.claim: Having registered iSLA internationally in 2023, Huawei established a Japanese offshoot in August 2025 and launched the NearLink Europe Partner Program in March 2026, with both efforts targeting the automotive sector specifically.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Automotive is the explicit beachhead for NearLink's European push; auto-sector suppliers and regulators should be the first to face disclosure and supply-chain scrutiny.
insights.quote: Having registered internationally in 2023, iSLA established a Japanese offshoot in August 2025 and the NearLink Europe Partner Program in March 2026, both targeting the automotive sector.
insights.locator: Huawei is seeking recognition for the technology as a global standard

insights.claim: Huawei is seeking recognition for NearLink as a global standard through bodies such as the UN-affiliated International Telecommunications Union (ITU).
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: A successful ITU standardization push would legitimize NearLink globally and make exclusion by individual jurisdictions harder to justify or enforce.
insights.quote: Huawei is seeking recognition for the technology as a global standard, for instance through the UN-affiliated International Telecommunications Union (ITU).
insights.locator: Huawei is seeking recognition for the technology as a global standard

insights.claim: Unlike the more confrontational international campaigns for WAPI or NewIP, NearLink is being promoted as a technology that can coexist with Bluetooth and Wi-Fi, with Huawei supporting interoperability and opening parts of the technology stack to developers to lower entry barriers and dilute the perception that it is a purely proprietary corporate technology.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: A coexistence rather than confrontation strategy makes NearLink harder to resist politically, since it does not force an explicit choice against existing Western standards.
insights.quote: Unlike more confrontational campaigns for WAPI or NewIP, NearLink is being promoted as a technology that can co exist with Bluetooth and Wi Fi.
insights.locator: Huawei is seeking recognition for the technology as a global standard

themes.theme: EU regulatory options and recommended response

insights.claim: The EU already has most of the tools needed to manage NearLink-related risks and only needs to use them.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: This is an actionable policy call: the binding constraint is political will and enforcement, not a legislative gap, so watch for EU implementation moves rather than new lawmaking.
insights.quote: The EU has most of the tools needed to manage the risks associated with NearLink – it only needs to use them.
insights.locator: The EU has tools needed to manage risks associated with NearLink

insights.claim: The EU's Digital Networks Act and Cyber Resilience Act already promote supply-chain transparency by requiring software bills of materials and lifecycle cybersecurity plans.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Companies selling connected devices into the EU should already be preparing software bills of materials that would expose embedded NearLink components.
insights.quote: The Digital Networks Act and the Cyber Resilience Act promote supply-chain transparency by requiring software bills of materials and lifecycle cybersecurity plans.
insights.locator: The EU has tools needed to manage risks associated with NearLink

insights.claim: The European Commission should uphold its proposed amendment to the Cybersecurity Act despite opposition from China, parts of industry, and legal challenges, in order to close remaining supply-chain governance gaps.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Watch for the fate of the Cybersecurity Act amendment as a bellwether for whether the EU will actually act on component-level China tech risk or let political pressure stall it.
insights.quote: the European Commission should uphold its proposed amendment to the Cybersecurity Act, despite opposition from China, parts of industry and legal challenges.
insights.locator: The EU has tools needed to manage risks associated with NearLink

insights.claim: The proposed Cybersecurity Act amendment would let Brussels classify embedded short-range connectivity as part of the security chain in critical sectors, designate NearLink-capable modules as sensitive components, and require disclosure of embedded stacks, combined with a coordinated EU position in global standard-setting forums.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: If enacted, this creates a concrete compliance obligation for any device maker or importer using NearLink modules in the EU, comparable to bill-of-materials rules already emerging elsewhere.
insights.quote: This would allow Brussels to classify embedded short range connectivity as part of the security chain in critical sectors, designate NearLink capable modules as sensitive components, and require the disclosure of embedded stacks.
insights.locator: The EU has tools needed to manage risks associated with NearLink

insights.claim: The recommended approach would bring NearLink under a governance model resembling China's own cybersecurity reviews: not an outright ban on foreign technology, but a structured mechanism to identify, assess and, where necessary, constrain its role in Europe's critical systems.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: This signals a review-and-constrain model rather than a blanket ban, meaning NearLink-linked companies could retain EU market access under compliance conditions rather than facing exclusion.
insights.quote: this would bring NearLink under a governance model that resembles China’s own cybersecurity reviews: not an outright ban on foreign technology, but a structured mechanism to identify, assess and, where necessary, constrain its role in Europe’s critical systems.
insights.locator: The EU has tools needed to manage risks associated with NearLink

insights.claim: Europe cannot afford to hesitate until NearLink presents it with another "Huawei moment" and needs to address the risk of a new strategic dependency now.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: The author's closing call to action frames NearLink policy as time-sensitive; delayed EU action raises the eventual cost and disruption of any later restriction, similar to the belated Huawei 5G response.
insights.quote: Europe cannot hesitate until NearLink presents it with another "Huawei moment" – it needs to address the risk of a new strategic dependency now.
insights.locator: The EU has tools needed to manage risks associated with NearLink
